d:
Balance over time for one account. Device is the only axis.

A credit card's balance is already ≤ 0, so plotting it as-is draws what is owed growing downward, and the series takes the debt hue. That is the whole of it — there is no second series.

2026-09-02 · Series=Single|Dual was DELETED. Dual's legend read "Cupo · Deuda", and cupo is limit − debt against a limit that does not move, so the second area was the first one mirrored: two shapes, one number. Measured before removing it: four instances in the file, all four inside this component's own documentation, none on a screen. Dev asked what number Dual plotted, which was the right question — the description named the picture and never the quantity. If a real second quantity ever exists, the axis comes back with a reason attached.

Both series carry a gradient that fades to fully transparent — account-chart/series/*/fill-to is the same hue at 0 alpha, not white — so the fill never turns milky over a dark canvas.

The marker line is account-chart/marker/line: slate on light, white at 70% on dark, because one fixed grey disappears against one of the two.

2026-09-01 · the static "Últimos 30 días" label was removed from the header. The range is now stated by chart-range, the strip of pills under the chart, and the axis already prints the dates. A fixed label would have contradicted both the moment anyone picked a different range — and a label that can contradict the control next to it is worse than no label.

State=Default and State=Hover: the tooltip and its marker were always drawn, which made a transient readout look like furniture. They now belong to Hover, the same axis TrendChart and EgresosCategoryChart carry, so the three charts of the system say hover the same way.

The year’s gross, split into what it turned into: Obligaciones · Provisiones · Gastos · Neto libre. Four segments of chart/categorical/1–4 — the same four as TrendChart and DistribucionCard, so the three say the same thing with the same colours.

220 across with a 30 ring. The track underneath is bg/surface/subtle, so the ring still reads as a whole when one segment is a sliver.

The centre is the readout, which is why this donut needs neither legend nor tooltip: by default it holds the gross, and selecting a segment moves that segment’s amount into the centre in its own colour while the others drop to 25%. Dimming the rest rather than lighting the one keeps the selected colour true — the colour is what names the segment.

Each segment is a control with a name, a role and a key. Without that the amounts it reveals are mouse-only: unreachable by keyboard and unannounced to a screen reader.

It appears only when there is more than one segment with an amount. A donut of one colour is a circle.

The centre figure is Amount/Hero, 28, and it is ABBREVIATED: up to two decimals and a lowercase unit — «$54,57 m» for millions, «$1,20 k» for thousands. Alfredo's call, 2026-09-12. A year's gross written in full is eleven digits inside a 160 circle; either it shrinks until it stops being the headline, or it wraps. The decimal separator is the comma, es-CO, like every other figure in the app. The abbreviation stops at the centre: the axis labels stay «$12M», uppercase and without decimals, because an axis is a scale you read against and this is the figure you read.

How one month’s expenses split across categories, as a single bar. One segment per category with an amount above zero, sorted widest first — so the bar has as many segments as the month had categories, not a fixed number. It is NOT DistribucionCard: that one always draws the same four segments (Obligaciones · Provisiones · Gastos · Neto libre) and answers where the gross income went. This answers what the expenses were made of.

8px tall, fully rounded, 1px gaps. Segment colour is category/<name>/accent — the same token as the category’s icon bubble and its row, so a category cannot be one colour in the list and another in the bar.

The legend is not decoration: it carries the percentage, which the bar alone cannot give you at a glance below ~10%. Label in Body/Small on fg/subtle, percentage in Amount/Small on fg/default — the figure is the emphasized half of the pair.

State=Hovered dims every OTHER segment and legend item to 30% and reveals the hovered category’s amount in pesos. Dimming the rest rather than highlighting the one keeps the hovered segment at its true colour, which matters when the colour is the identity.

Sits under the expense list, separated by a 1px rule on border/default and 12 of padding. It renders nothing at all when the month’s total is zero — an empty rounded bar reads as a component that failed to load.

Two things the mock cannot show and the code decides: segment widths are the real percentages (here 34,2 · 21,5 · 15,8 · 11,4 · 9,6 · 7,5), and the legend wraps — two rows at 640, three at 346, with the hovered amount taking its own right-aligned line on mobile because it does not fit beside the last item.

Legend entry for the annual donut and the 8-month trend bars.

Colour comes from chart/categorical/1–5, which alias the KPI tokens — so a legend swatch can never drift from the KPI it labels.

The date range of an account chart — the strip of pills under it, the pattern every stocks app uses.

It composes Segment instances rather than minting a pill of its own. Segment’s own description says a segment on its own is not a control; this is one of the controls that composes them, the same relationship tab-navigation has with Tab. Selected therefore reuses Segment’s Selected — bg/brand-alpha-20 with border/brand-alpha-50 — so “selected” means the same thing here as in every other control in the file.

THE STRIP IS VARIABLE LENGTH, AND THAT IS THE RULE, NOT A CONVENIENCE. A range is rendered only when the account has at least one movement OLDER than that range’s start. Otherwise it draws exactly the same line as the shorter range beside it, and a control that cannot change what you see is not a choice — it is a promise the data does not keep. Alfredo’s call, 2026-09-01, and it is the reason the full seven can be offered at all.

Two of the seven need something the data model does not guarantee. `date` is OPTIONAL on an income (src/types), so an account whose movements only carry a month has no day-level series at all: 1D and 1S cannot be drawn for it and must not be offered. 5A waits the same way — the app is younger than five years, so the pill appears the first time an account is.

That is why this is a strip of instances and not a variant axis. Its length is data, not design, exactly as tab-navigation’s is (Tributarias and Provisiones only exist when the user enabled those groups) and action-chip’s is (only categories with data that month).

AccountChart lost its static “Últimos 30 días” label the day this arrived. The strip now states the range, the axis already prints the dates, and a fixed label would have contradicted both the moment anyone picked 1A.

OPEN — two copy choices Alfredo should settle: “1S” for the week (mirrors the reference’s 1W; “7D” is less ambiguous in Spanish) and “YTD”, kept as the acronym Colombian finance uses, where “Año” would be plainer.

The pills are 32 high, like every Segment. That clears 2.5.8 (24) and not 2.5.5 (44); it is the height the rest of the system already uses for this control, so changing it is a decision about Segment, not about this strip.

The year month by month, each bar stacked by expense CATEGORY rather than by KPI — this is what the money was spent ON; TrendChart is what the month was made of.

220 tall over 172 of plot, twelve bands, segments in category/<name>/accent so a category is the same colour here, in its row and in category-bar.

Empty months are drawn as a 4px stub on chart/empty, not left out. A year that hides its empty months compresses time and puts March next to June as though they were adjacent — and the gap IS information: it says the app was not being used yet.

The code cannot draw that today. visibleData filters months without data before the branch that draws the stub, so the branch is unreachable and chart/empty has no consumer until the filter goes. That is the one behavioural change this drawing asks for.

The average line sits ON TOP of the bars, dashed 4,4 at 1.5, on chart/average — six rungs above the grid because it is a figure you read against. The code draws it before the bars, so a tall stack swallows it.

Its tooltip is not TooltipReadout: it is a hand-built panel with a per-category list and a «Promedio» footer. Two charts on one page with two different tooltips is a defect, and the fix belongs in the library rather than in either chart.

State=Hover uses the same Tooltip · TooltipReadout as TrendChart, with a Divider row for «Promedio». That unifies the two tooltips of the page, which today are two different things. Its swatches are the CATEGORY accents, and there they fail: measured on the inverted surface they are 3.45–5.02 in Light and 1.32–1.80 in Dark. In dark mode those dots are invisible. The fix is a category swatch family fixed at the light accent — 14 tokens — and it is not minted yet, so the Dark preview shows the defect on purpose.

State=Empty is the year with no expenses: title, one line of explanation and no action. The action that the Empty component brings by default is hidden — there is nothing to add from a chart.

Only the TOP segment of a stack is rounded — radius/4 on its two top corners, everything below square (Alfredo, 2026-09-12): rounding every segment turns one bar into a stack of separate pills and the eye stops adding them up. The empty-month stub carries radius/4 on all four corners, which at 4px tall makes it a dash with round ends — a deliberate mark rather than a bar that was cut off.

The last eight months, each one a stacked bar: Obligaciones · Provisiones · Gastos · Neto libre, bottom to top — the order in which a month stops being yours.

252 tall over 180 of plot; each bar takes 68% of its band. Series bind to chart/categorical/1–4 rather than to the KPI tokens directly. Same value today, and that is the point: the indirection is what stops a series drifting from the card it corresponds to.

The band behind a column is the month the rest of the app is showing (chart/highlight), and clicking a bar moves the app to that month. These bars are a control, not a picture — which is why the current one has to be marked at all.

Four dashed rungs on chart/grid, faint on purpose: the bars are the figure and the grid is only there when you look for it. Hover opens a Tooltip with TooltipReadout, whose swatches are readout/swatch/*, a separate rung chosen to clear 3:1 on the inverted surface — the chart colours do not (tax measures 1.44 there).

On Mobile the labels drop the year. Eight «sep ’26» do not fit in 346 and nothing wraps them: they overlap. Measured on the real width, not assumed.

Two series disappear for an employee profile (Obligaciones, Provisiones), leaving two. Not drawn as a variant: it is the same bar with fewer segments, and an axis for it would double the set to say nothing new.

State=Hover is the tooltip: Tooltip · Side=Top with a TooltipReadout inside and one ReadoutRow per series, swatches on readout/swatch/* — a separate rung from the chart colours, chosen to clear 3:1 on the inverted surface, where the chart colours do not.

Only the TOP segment of a stack is rounded — radius/4 on its two top corners, everything below square. Alfredo's call, 2026-09-12. Rounding every segment turns one bar into a stack of separate pills and the eye stops adding them up; rounding only the top says «this is one quantity, and it ends here».
